Question Choices: Select. What can be concluded about opposite sides of a parallelogram? ~~They must have different measures | No relationship is guaranteed | They are congruent~~
Hints: A diagonal creates two congruent triangles.|Use CPCTC on the opposite sides.
Solution: Opposite sides are parallel by the definition of parallelogram. A diagonal creates two congruent triangles by alternate interior angles and their shared side (ASA); corresponding opposite sides are therefore congruent.

Question Choices: Select. What do the diagonals of a parallelogram do to each other? ~~They are always perpendicular | They always have equal lengths | They bisect each other~~
Hints: Their intersection is the midpoint of each diagonal.|Each diagonal is split in half.
Solution: A parallelogram has half-turn symmetry about its diagonal intersection. The half-turn exchanges the endpoints of each diagonal, so the intersection is the midpoint of both. Thus the diagonals bisect each other. A rhombus is also a parallelogram.

Question Choices: Select. What can be concluded about opposite angles of a parallelogram? ~~They must have different measures | No relationship is guaranteed | They are congruent~~
Hints: A diagonal creates congruent triangles.|Use corresponding angles.
Solution: Opposite sides are parallel. Each of two opposite angles is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so they have equal measures and are congruent.

Question Choices: Two consecutive angles of a parallelogram measure x and 110 degrees. Find x. Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Solution: Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary. The missing angle is 180 - 110 = 70 degrees.
